nodes.summary: Algorithms and statistical models on biological sequences and data: sequence alignment, genome assembly, motifs, RNA secondary structure, clustering and network reconstruction.
nodes.title: Bioinformatics

nodes.summary: Mathematical models for tumour sequencing data: purity and copy number, cancer cell fractions, mutation detection power, mutational signatures and the timing of genomic events.
nodes.title: Cancer genomics

nodes.summary: Backward-in-time models of the genealogy of a sample of genes, from Kingman's coalescent and its generalizations to the site frequency spectrum, recombination and population structure.
nodes.title: Coalescent theory

nodes.summary: Statistical tests of neutrality and genome scans for selection based on polymorphism, divergence and haplotype structure, and models of the distribution of fitness effects.
nodes.title: Detecting natural selection

nodes.summary: Compartmental, renewal and branching-process models of infectious disease transmission and their reproduction numbers.
nodes.title: Mathematical epidemiology

nodes.summary: Reaction–diffusion models of biological spread and spatial patterning, including travelling waves, morphogen gradients and Turing instabilities.
nodes.title: Reaction–diffusion and pattern formation

nodes.summary: Reconstruction of evolutionary trees from sequence data: substitution models, likelihood and parsimony, distance methods, tree metrics, splits and the enumeration of phylogenetic trees.
nodes.title: Phylogenetics

nodes.summary: Differential-equation models of population growth, species interaction and evolutionary change, such as logistic growth, predator–prey systems, replicator dynamics and quasispecies.
nodes.title: Population and evolutionary dynamics

nodes.summary: Mathematical models of allele frequencies in populations under random mating, selection, mutation, migration and genetic drift, including the Wright–Fisher and Moran models and their diffusion limits.
nodes.title: Population genetics

nodes.summary: f-statistics, admixture graphs, ancestry models and linkage-disequilibrium methods for inferring the relationships and mixture histories of populations.
nodes.title: Population structure and admixture

nodes.summary: The genetics of continuously varying traits: decomposition of genetic variance, resemblance between relatives, kinship, mixed models and the response to selection.
nodes.title: Quantitative genetics

nodes.summary: Statistical methods for genome-wide association studies, heritability estimation from summary statistics, fine-mapping, Mendelian randomization and gene constraint scores.
nodes.title: Statistical genetics

nodes.summary: Dynamics of biochemical reaction networks and gene regulatory circuits: mass-action kinetics, enzyme kinetics, ultrasensitivity, feedback, metabolic flux analysis and gene expression noise.
nodes.title: Systems biology

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
